qualifications: Historical vs. current vs. underwritten are kept separate and are not interchangeable: T12 (2025-09-01 to 2026-08-31) EGI 723,600 / NOI before reserves 507,600 / NCF 498,400; current contractual rent roll 49,100/mo (=589,200 annualized) at 87.5% by count and 87.83% by area as of 2026-08-31; supplied underwriting scenario (Sept 2026 forward) EGI 768,144 / NOI 544,218.24 / NCF 539,618.24. Per Property-and-Plan.pdf p.1, historical income is not forced to a point-in-time annualized rent roll.

Rent-roll/lease conflict resolved in favor of the executed instrument: Rent-Roll.xlsx G7 shows $7,000 for suite 101 and is expressly stale (note C19); the amendment signed 2026-07-20 and effective 2026-08-01 sets $7,500. This raises contractual monthly base by $500 (+$6,000/yr) but does NOT flow into underwritten revenue, which uses the plan's supplied gross potential rent.
Unsigned 2026-08-27 broker proposal ($8,000/mo, term through 2033-08-31) is excluded from every figure; it is not an amendment (Lease-File.pdf p.1 Sec. 6, p.2).

Unresolved evidence: the plan's supplied UW gross potential base rent of $657,600 exceeds both T12 GPR ($645,600) and the rent roll's gross potential at contractual+market rents ($49,100 contractual + $5,200 market for vacant suite 108 = $54,300/mo = $651,600/yr) by $6,000/yr. Source of the difference is not explained in the packet; it was used as instructed but should be re-derived before credit approval.

Also unresolved: the same $27,600 insurance figure is described as an insurer 'renewal confirmation' (Insurance evidence row) and as a 'renewal quote' (expense table) in Property-and-Plan.pdf p.2, and no insurer document is attached. If it is only a quote, insurance is unverified and UW NOI is exposed by the $2,400 step-up from the T12 actual.

T12 statement contains no 'property NOI' subtotal; the pre-emptive caution in Property-and-Plan.pdf p.1 about reserves being labeled 'property NOI' therefore did not require restatement. Reserves ($9,200), capital improvements ($98,000), loan P&I ($294,000) and depreciation ($180,000) were verified as below-the-line and excluded from operating expenses. Monthly columns on T12-Statement.pdf pp.1-2 foot to the printed Annual column for every line checked.

Sizing used unrounded intermediates; displayed currency is rounded for readers. The maximum loan is $5,327,927.5 before display rounding; small differences (a few dollars) can arise from the number of decimals carried in the 0.08102486 debt constant.

First-year contractual debt service ($421,760, at the 6.25% contract rate, 0-month IO) is $9,934 LOWER than the sizing debt service ($431,694.59, at the 6.50% sizing floor). Actual first-year DSCR on UW NCF is therefore ~1.28x versus the 1.25x sizing test. Sizing DSCR remains the binding test.
Debt yield at the maximum loan is 10.21% (>9.00% minimum) and LTV is 63.6% (5,327,927 / 8,372,588 < 65.00%), consistent with DSCR being the binding constraint.

The $8,372,588 capitalized value is an indicative underwriting computation from the plan's scenario NOI and the lender's stated 6.50% cap rate. No appraisal, market comps, environmental report, sponsor track record or credit approval is in the packet (Property-and-Plan.pdf p.1; Lender-Terms.pdf p.1 'no appraisal is implied'). Lender terms are nonbinding indicative terms dated 2026-09-01.

Suite 108 (2,800 SF, 10.3% of area) is vacant with $5,200/mo market rent shown for context only; it generates no current contractual income (Rent-Roll.xlsx C17). Suite 106 (5,000 SF, $10,500/mo - the largest rent) expires 2027-08-31, inside the 60-month loan term, and is the principal near-term rollover exposure; combined with the plan's 6.00% revenue-loss assumption this is the main sensitivity driver.
Security deposit ($15,000) is a liability, not income; excluded from EGI and from cash-to-borrower.

Cash-to-borrower assumes no fee capitalization, interest reserve, cash sweep, earn-out or holdback (Lender-Terms.pdf p.1) and only the two stated transaction costs (payoff $3,400,000; fixed closing costs $48,000). Prorations, escrow funding, title, legal and reserve deposits are not quantified in the packet and would reduce net cash.

Cap-rate sensitivity requested for the workbook (+50 bps to 7.00%) is not a binding-constraint change here: value would fall to $7,774,546 and the LTV limit to $5,053,455, which would become the binding constraint (below the $5,327,927 DSCR limit) - i.e., loan proceeds would drop ~5.2% to ~$5,053,455 on cap-rate movement alone, all else equal.

No source in this packet was unreadable; all five documents (Lease-File.pdf, Lender-Terms.pdf, Property-and-Plan.pdf, Rent-Roll.xlsx, T12-Statement.pdf) yielded text. All parties, addresses and figures are fictional evaluation material; nothing was geocoded, researched externally or inferred from outside comps.

These are the plan's scenario inputs, not lender-approved forecasts.
summary: Deliverable 1 (extraction/analysis) and Deliverable 2 (loan sizing) are complete above. Historical T12 (2025-09-01 to 2026-08-31): EGI $723,600, operating expenses $216,000, NOI before reserves $507,600, reserves $9,200, NCF $498,400. Current contractual position at 2026-08-31: 8 suites, 7 occupied, 23,000 SF total / 20,200 SF occupied (87.5% by count, 87.83% by area); rent roll as printed $48,600/mo, $49,100/mo after the executed 2026-07-20 first amendment that raises suite 101 to $7,500/mo effective 2026-08-01 (expiry unchanged at 2031-08-31, deposit $15,000, renewal option NOT exercised, unsigned $8,000/mo broker proposal excluded). Supplied underwriting scenario: EGI $768,144, management fee $30,725.76 (4% of UW EGI beats $24,000 T12 actual), operating expenses $223,925.76, NOI before reserves $544,218.24, reserves $4,600, NCF $539,618.24; indicative value at the lender's 6.50% cap rate $8,372,588. Sizing at the 6.50% sizing floor (25-yr monthly amortization, annual constant 0.0810249): LTV limit $5,442,182, DSCR limit $5,327,927, debt-yield limit $6,046,869 - maximum loan $5,327,927 with DSCR binding at 1.25x, resulting debt yield 10.21% and LTV 63.6%. Sizing debt service $431,695; actual first-year contractual debt service at the 6.25% contract rate with 0-month IO is $421,760 (actual first-year DSCR ~1.28x). Net cash OUT to the borrower is approximately $1,826,648 after the $3,400,000 payoff, $53,279 (1.00%) origination fee and $48,000 fixed closing costs, so the cash-out refinance is feasible on these indicative terms. Downside: with EGI -5% (management recomputed to $29,189, other expenses held) UW NOI falls to $507,347 and NCF to $502,747; adding a 100 bp higher sizing rate (7.50%, cap rate held at 6.50%) reduces the maximum loan to about $4,535,439 - still DSCR-bound and $792,488 (-14.9%) below base - which would cut net cash out to roughly $1,042,085 on the same cost stack. Prepayment friction is 1% of outstanding principal in years 1-2 only, with no swap and therefore no breakage cost. Key watch items for internal review: the unexplained $6,000/yr gap between the plan's scenario gross potential rent and the rent roll/market build-up, the confirmation-versus-quote ambiguity on the $27,600 insurance renewal, the 2027-08-31 expiry of the property's largest rent (suite 106, $10,500/mo), and the vacant 2,800 SF suite 108. Deliverables 3 (XLSX workbook) and 4 (PDF/native memorandum) were NOT produced - see 'blocked'. No file has been created or delivered in this workflow.
